newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to speed up sell-offs in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to speed up sell-offs in 1997.

text.p: Turkey is planning to speed up its sluggish privatisation programme in 1997, deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said.
"Privatisation will put its stamp on 1997," Ciller told reporters on late Thursday.
She said Turkey would finalise privatisation of two cement factories, a refractor and a ceramics plant belonging to cement group Citosan and 30-year leasing of eight state ports this month.

The government is also seeking to achieve "significant progress" this month on the privatisation of four ongoing projects -- tyre-maker Petlas, tourism firm Turban, flat steel producer Eregli and Etibank which was split into three banks, Ciller said.
Sell-off negotiations are expected to begin in Etibank, Petlas and Turban soon and bids will be received for Eregli, put on sale in December, by January 27, officials say.
Turkey has raised $3 billion since 1986 when the privatisation programme started.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition government aims to raise some $15 billion through the sale and lease of state assets, including power plants and part of telecommunications company Turk Telekom, worth $3.5 billion.

Turkey appointed a consortium headed by Goldman Sachs to run the sale of Turk Telekom shares in December. The government hopes to put some 10 to 15 percent of Turk Telekom on sale in the first quarter of 1997.
